content_sections.body: Useful actions: get up, eat breakfast, study, work, go home, sleep. Put the action after I or you.
content_sections.title: Routine verbs

content_sections.body:
A: What do you do in the morning?
B: I get up and eat breakfast. What do you do?
A: I study.
content_sections.title: What do you do?

exercises.prompt: Put the fictional morning routine in a sensible order.

items.prompt: A: What do you do in the morning?  B: ___

exercises.prompt: Describe three actions in your real or imagined day, in order.
exercises.rubric: Uses three verbs from the lesson.; Forms present-simple I statements accurately.; Presents the actions in a clear order.

objectives: Use common verbs for a simple daily routine.
Make present-simple statements with I and you and ask What do you do?

constraints: Use only this lesson's routine verbs.
Use no external recording or passage.
listening.goal: Practise the listening target for this lesson.
listening.instruction: Read an original three-action morning routine once slowly. Ask the learner to put the actions in order, then read it again and reveal the script.

constraints: If no audio is available, state NOT_ASSESSED and provide stress marks only.
Do not assess from typed text.
pronunciation.goal: Practise the pronunciation target for this lesson.
pronunciation.instruction: Model get up, eat breakfast, study, and go home with clear word stress. Ask the learner to repeat each phrase and combine two with and.

constraints: Limit correction to present-simple I/you forms and target verbs.
speaking.goal: Practise the speaking target for this lesson.
speaking.instruction: Ask What do you do in the morning? Wait for the answer, ask one follow-up about another part of the day, and model one short fictional answer if help is needed.

constraints: Do not add advanced time expressions.
Do not rewrite the entire routine.
writing.goal: Practise the writing target for this lesson.
writing.instruction: Ask the learner to draft four ordered sentences about a real or fictional day. Give up to two corrections on subject-verb form or verb choice, then ask for a revision.

title: Everyday Actions
